parsed.summary: This paper introduces CLASVS, a continuous-latent autoregressive model for melody-preserving lyric editing in singing voice synthesis. It utilizes State-Control-Transition (SCT) routing and Progressive State-Control Grounding (PSCG) to resolve the conflict between target lyrics and reference melody without requiring paired counterfactual edit recordings. The model achieves a 46.2% reduction in macro-phoneme error rate (macro-PER) compared to the discrete-AR Vevo2 baseline while maintaining high naturalness and lyric intelligibility.

chk_problem.value: Removing score annotations in melody-preserving lyric editing creates a selective-preservation problem where the model must retain reference performance characteristics while rejecting source lyrics.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Removing score annotations, however, creates a selective-preservation problem: the model must retain the performance characteristics carried by the reference while rejecting its source lyrics.

chk_method.value: CLASVS uses State-Control-Transition (SCT) routing to separate global lyric planning from local acoustic continuity, and Progressive State-Control Grounding (PSCG) to learn this routing without paired counterfactual edit recordings.
chk_method.paper_quote: Its State–Control–Transition (SCT) routing keeps target-lyric and reference-melody controls persistent, returns semantic feedback on phonetic progress to the causal planner, and confines the previous latent patch to the local Transition.

chk_data.value: The model is trained on approximately 8,000 hours of Mandarin singing, 2,000 hours of Mandarin Emilia speech, and 300 hours of curated open-source singing.
chk_data.paper_quote: Training audio comprises about 8,000 hours of permission-documented Mandarin singing, 2,000 hours of Mandarin Emilia speech (He et al. 2024), and 300 hours of curated open-source singing; all data are Mandarin.

chk_setup.value: The experimental setup uses three 120K-update seeds trained with BF16, ZeRO-2, AdamW, and a global batch size of 128.
chk_setup.paper_quote: Three 120K-update seeds use BF16, ZeRO-2, AdamW, and global batch 128.

chk_primary_result.value: CLASVS reduces macro-PER by 46.2% compared to the discrete-AR Vevo2 baseline across two Mandarin benchmarks.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: On two Mandarin benchmarks, CLASVS improves all four operations over discrete-AR Vevo2 and reduces macro-PER by 46.2%, while maintaining melody, singer similarity, and perceptual quality.

chk_secondary_result.value: CLASVS improves naturalness (N-MOS) by +.48 and lyric intelligibility (L-MOS) by +.32 over the continuous-NAR comparator YingMusic+.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: CLASVS improves N-MOS by +.48 [+.34, +.62] and L-MOS by +.32 [+.20, +.44] over YingMusic+ under the same listening protocol; M-MOS differs by an undetectable +.01.

chk_baseline.value: The primary baseline is Vevo2, a discrete autoregressive model, and the complementary baseline is YingMusic+, a continuous non-autoregressive model.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: Vevo2 is the primary comparator because it shares CLASVS’s sequential interface but predicts discrete acoustic tokens rather than continuous AudioVAE latent patches (Zhang et al. 2026).

chk_conclusion.value: CLASVS successfully establishes continuous-latent autoregression for melody-preserving Mandarin lyric editing without requiring manual score annotations.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: CLASVS establishes continuous-latent autoregression for melody-preserving Mandarin lyric editing without manual score annotations.

chk_limitation.value: The evaluation is limited to a single recognizer and reference-timing metrics on Mandarin 2–6-syllable edits, leaving cross-lingual and long-edit validation as open challenges.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Evaluation uses one recognizer and reference-timing metrics on Mandarin 2–6-syllable edits; cross-lingual and long-edit validation remain open.
